title: On an open question about the equivalence of monotone maximality and surjectivity condition in $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces: Negative and partially positive answers
summary: In a Hilbert space, it is known that a monotone operator is maximal if and only if the \emph{surjectivity condition}, \ie its resolvent has a full domain, holds. This equivalence is an open question in a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space, knowing only that the surjectivity condition implies the monotone maximality. In fact, there have been three approaches to generalize the monotonicity from a Hilbert space into a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space $X$ --- \textbf{A:} the ones of dual space $X^{\ast}$, \textbf{B:} of linear dual space $X^{\diamond}$, and \textbf{C:} of tangent bundle $TX$.
